title: Tottenham Hotspur seek reinforcements after Newcastle United match
seoTitle: Tottenham seek reinforcements after Newcastle match
subtitle: Roberto De Zerbi's side registered a lackluster offensive performance in their first home game of the season
excerpt: Tottenham Hotspur are monitoring the transfer market after their offensive performance against Newcastle United in the Premier League.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Tottenham Hotspur drew attention by ending the first half of their home match against Newcastle United without finding the back of the net, prompting assessments regarding the need for new signings. Manager Roberto De Zerbi pointed out limitations in the attacking sector and indicated that the team could seek new players before the transfer window closes.

Attacking performance prompts reflection

During the Premier League match, the home side dominated possession in the opening half but failed to translate pressure into effective shots against the goal defended by Lukas Hornicek. The best chance of the first half came from Pedro Porro, who shot over the crossbar from a distance of 12 yards. The lack of creativity and the wingers' inability to beat their markers highlighted gaps in the final third of the pitch.

Transfer market movements

The board made significant investments during the signing period, bringing in names like Savio and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. Despite spending totaling three hundred million pounds in the summer, the coaching staff is evaluating the possibility of seeking one more reinforcement for a specific position. Discussions involve the owner, sporting director Johan Lange, chief executive Vinai Venkatesham, and Enrico Venturelli.

Absences and squad planning

The starting lineup featured reinforcements such as Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes alongside Marmoush, while Savio was left out due to muscle fatigue after a Carabao Cup match. Other players like Kevin Danso, Pape Matar Sarr, and Richarlison were left out of the squad. The situation of players who have expressed a desire to leave and are awaiting offers also remains on the club management's radar.

Premier League table situation

In the competition table, Tottenham Hotspur occupies twentieth place with no points accumulated after the first matches played. The club remains attentive to the final movements of the market to define arrivals and departures in the professional squad until the window closes.

With information from AOL.co.uk, BBC, The Guardian.
